title: Row-delta commits and multi-table transactions in iceberg-rust: patterns from a CDC producer
summary: Steve, building a Postgres-to-Iceberg CDC pipeline on iceberg-rust, opened two draft PRs for discussion: a RowDeltaAction that commits data files and equality or position delete files in one snapshot, and multi-table transaction commits through the REST `transactions/commit` endpoint. Andrei Tserakhau shared lessons from doing the same in iceberg-go: choose the operation type from the content, apply equality deletes only to data files with a strictly lower sequence number, expect most effort on the read side, and reject empty or float/double equality keys. For multi-table commits he advised a separate optional trait, reloading after the 204 response, and treating 5xx responses as commit-state-unknown. Steve applied several points and noted that his `prepare_commit` consumes the transaction. Andrei agreed that consuming is the right default in Rust and pointed to the iceberg-go changes for partition-scoped conflict detection and removal of dangling equality deletes. The PRs remained drafts in the thread.

positions.stance: Proposes adding RowDeltaAction and REST multi-table transaction commits to iceberg-rust and is willing to adapt the APIs to the ongoing merge-on-read work.
Keep multi-table commit as a separate optional trait implemented by REST, split building a commit from committing it, and never blindly retry 5xx responses because the commit state is unknown.
`prepare_commit` should consume the transaction, because Rust ownership then prevents a prepared transaction from also being committed directly.
Consuming the transaction is the right default and fits the commit-state-unknown error model; iceberg-go needed a manual committed flag to get the same guarantee.

outcome.note: Design feedback was exchanged and partly applied to the draft PRs; the thread records no decision on merging them.

why_it_matters: It collects correctness pitfalls for row-delta and multi-table commits that iceberg-go already hit and that the iceberg-rust write path will need to handle.
